newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut GOP to hold Senate, Gov. Rowland says.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut GOP to hold Senate, Gov. Rowland says.

text.p: Connecticut Republican Gov. John Rowland predicted Tuesday morning that Republicans would hold their slim majority in the state Senate but Democrats would retain control of the state House.
"We're not going to take the House, although I'd love to see it happen," Rowland told Reuters after casting his vote at the Annie Fisher School at mid-morning.
Republicans hold a 19-17 majority in the state Senate, while Democrats enjoy an overwhelming 92-59 control of the house.
Every seat in the state legislature is up for grabs, but there are no U.S. Senate or gubernatorial races in Connecticut this year.

"My guess is you'll see a pretty strong re-election effort (by both parties)," Rowland said. "Two years ago, it was time for a change. (But) things are going fairly well in the state, so I think you're going to see a 98 percent re-election factor."

Asked about the Republicans' chances nationally, Rowland said, "I think we will increase in the Senate, and I think we will hold the House. Whatever happens at the top (presidential race) happens - that all depends on who gets their vote out."

He said Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole made a "valiant effort" but "the polls hurt, because after four months of watching the polls, the stories become the polls rather than the issues. It becomes a fait accompli, almost."
He added, "But having said that, there could be some upsets."
